meta.title: Dashboard User Guide
meta.subtitle: Clinic Admissions Dashboard
meta.big_idea: This guide shows facility leaders how to read the admissions dashboard, pull the right report and avoid common mistakes.
meta.notes: Synthetic example for the skill self-test. Not a real dashboard.

slides.title: What This Guide Covers
slides.notes: Use this page to jump to the section you need; each section stands on its own.

slides.title: How to Use the Admissions Dashboard
slides.heading: Navigating the New Interface
paragraphs: This guide gives a quick overview of the admissions dashboard and the steps to pull, read and act on your clinic's numbers.
The goal is to let facility leaders answer their own admissions questions without waiting for ad hoc reports.
Before you start, confirm your access request was approved so every filter shows your facilities.
takeaways: Data refreshes every morning by 6 a.m.
Every page follows the same filters
slides.notes: Set expectations first: what the dashboard is for and what access you need before the workflow section.

slides.title: The Main View Has Four Zones
slides.intro: The main view is split into four zones so you can find filters, numbers and exports quickly.
slides.alt: Admissions dashboard main view with navigation, KPI ribbon, chart canvas and export tools marked A to D.

zones.label: Global Navigation
zones.detail: Facility selector, date range and profile settings

zones.label: KPI Ribbon
zones.detail: Headline numbers for the last 30 days against target

zones.label: Chart Canvas
zones.detail: Admission trends and variance by week

zones.label: Export Tools
zones.detail: PDF and CSV downloads in the top-right corner

slides.notes: Walk the four zones in order; the letters on the screenshot match the cards.

slides.title: Pull a Report in Four Steps

nodes.label: Select Parameters
nodes.detail: Set date range and facilities in the top bar

nodes.label: Apply Filters
nodes.detail: Choose the patient group or clinic type

nodes.label: Preview Data
nodes.detail: Check the on-screen table before exporting

nodes.label: Export Report
nodes.detail: Download the CSV with your filters applied

slides.alt: Four steps on a line from selecting parameters to exporting the report, alternating above and below.
slides.notes: Most mistakes happen at step one, so it is highlighted.

slides.title: Three Things to Know Before You Export

cards.title: Use Month-end Dates
cards.text: For the monthly admissions report, choose End of Month, not Current Date, so the warehouse has finished its 48-hour reconciliation.

cards.title: Save Your View
cards.text: Use Save View on any widget to keep your filters and open the dashboard ready next time.

cards.title: Keep Exports Internal
cards.text: Never send exported CSV files by external email; patient-level data must stay on the secure network.

slides.notes: The warning is a compliance requirement, not a preference; repeat it in training.

slides.title: Read the Admissions Versus Discharges Chart
slides.heading: Admissions vs. Discharges
slides.intro: This chart compares daily admissions and discharges so you can spot capacity pressure early.
slides.alt: Admissions versus discharges chart with a rolling average line over daily bars.

annotations.text: The solid line is the 30-day rolling average, which smooths daily swings.
Click any bar to open the detail for that date.
Discharges run about 12 hours behind until physician sign-off.

slides.notes: Point out the 12-hour delay; it explains most questions about yesterday's numbers.

slides.title: Need Help With the Dashboard?
slides.text: Reach out to the sponsoring team for dashboard support.
slides.notes: Close with where to get help; there is no ask in a guide.
